text:
mike: seeing recurring cudaMalloc spikes in prod prowler runs when KV cache churn hits a hot keyset. latency SLOs blow up for ~200ms intervals.
olga: noticed those on canary earlier too. spikes line up with `kv_cache::evict_and_repack` calls in the trace.
sam: shared an nsys timeline (uploaded): perf-bot: /tmp/nsys/1802500123-kvspike.qdrep
mike: thanks — i pulled the timeline. host syncs (cudaMemcpyAsync -> cudaDeviceSynchronize) cluster around the same window.
ryan: do we have stack samples? sounds like the routing layer sends many concurrent requests to a single GPU which forces cache thrash + allocations.
olga: attaching a short perfetto snippet I grabbed — lots of small allocations followed by one big cudaMalloc (~8MB) repeatedly.
sam: short nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --output=kvspike --sample=cpu ./bin/serve --workload x
```
mike: i also see repeated `cudaFree`/`cudaMalloc` pairs rather than reusing pool allocations during the burst window.
ryan: that smells like pool fragmentation. are we returning chunks to the arena under load? config maybe too aggressive on slab shrink.
olga: current pool config in canary (snippet):
```
{ "slab_size": 64MB, "min_slab_retention": 2, "shrink_threshold_ratio": 0.15 }
```
sam: under high concurrent evictions we get interleaved frees causing fragmentation and fallback to `cudaMalloc` which triggers the slow path.
perf-bot: stack samples (top) in that window: `kv_cache::repack` -> `routing::handle_batch` -> `serve::dispatch` -> `cudaMalloc`
mike: interestingly the kernel timeline shows long gaps between kernels on that GPU while CPU is busy doing memory ops.
ryan: can we route hot-keys to a sticky GPU so we don't thrash the KV pool across devices? sticky routing would reduce cross-device evictions.
olga: sticky would help but we still need better pool behavior. two immediate remediation ideas:
- increase slab_size to reduce number of allocations
- enable cudaMallocAsync / cudaMemPool so frees are constant time and don't hit driver
sam: i tried a dev build with `cudaMallocAsync` and switched pool to use mempool APIs. microbenchmarks show 4x reduction in alloc latency under bursts.
mike: any compatibility concerns? we run mixed driver stack across customers.
ryan: cudaMallocAsync requires CUDA 11.3+ and specific driver support, and behavior differs with third-party libs. we should gate by capability.
olga: for short-term prod patch, propose: raise slab_size to 256MB for high-QPS routes + bump min_slab_retention to 4. also add a routing flag: `sticky_on_churn=true`.
sam: sample config patch I pushed to staging branch (link): https://git.internal/redwood/kvpool/commit/abcd1234
mike: can we add a perf test that simulates a hot keyset with concurrent eviction and measure `cudaMalloc` counts?
sam: yes — test harness change is small, will run against first dedicated canary set.
perf-bot: profiling note: when you upload qdrep, also capture the `nsys` exported `sqlite` to run `nvtx` queries, e.g.:
```
nsys export --output=kvspike.sqlite kvspike.qdrep
sqlite3 kvspike.sqlite "select * from nvtx_events where name like '%alloc%';"
```
mike: good tip. also from perfetto i saw many small memcpys back-to-back, maybe from object serialization while waiting on allocation.
ryan: action items:
- sam: add synthetic that reproduces hot-key allocation storm + track `cudaMalloc` counts (ETA: today)
- olga: apply slab_size bump to staging and enable sticky routing flag in a canary (ETA: tomorrow)
- mike: coordinate canary perf run and collect nsys/qdrep + sqlite (ETA: tomorrow afternoon)
- ryan: prototype mempool-enabled allocator wrapper with runtime capability check (ETA: EOW)
mike: i also want a temporary metric: gauge `runtime.alloc_path` tag `pool|malloc|mempool` so we can alert on leaky fallbacks.
olga: i'll add the metric in the pool code path.
sam: FYI: if we keep aggressive batching heuristics, sticky routing might cause imbalance. need to pair with adaptive batch sizing.
mike: noted. for now focus on stopping the OOM-like latency spikes.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: kvpool/staging -> canary-3 at 2026-03-18T11:20Z
sam: will upload the perf run once canary is live.
ryan: one more idea — add transient backoff in dispatch when we detect rapid alloc/free sequences; give pool a chance to coalesce.
mike: ok let's iterate. thanks team.
perf-bot: upload complete: /tmp/nsys/1802500123-kvspike.qdrep (size 12.4MB)
